thread:
maria: heads-up, I hit a correctness blip during a soft-evict handoff on canary. Two responses served for one request when the lease and handoff overlapped.
aj: ack, saw an alert. can you paste the minimal repro / logs?
maria: minimal trace below. basically: handoff kicks off, a read arrives, lease revokes, handoff completes -> old shard still serves because request already passed fastpath checks.
```
HANDOFF start prefix=acct-42 epoch=108
REQ id=0x7f enter -> check_pin(epoch=108) ok
LEASE revoke prefix=acct-42 epoch=109
HANDOFF commit -> ownership=shard-17
REQ id=0x7f served by old shard -> returned
```
kevin: hmm, that's the classic race: fastpath checks epoch then continues; if epoch advances mid-flight we get duplicate serve and later tombstone may cause inconsistent reads.
sara: we intentionally avoided blocking new pins during handoff to keep p99 down. but this shows a correctness surface we didn't fully quantify.
evans: can we add a micro-check before the final writeout? e.g., re-check epoch at response-send and fail fast if stale. cheap compare only.
aj: that's the same thought I had. runtime returns a soft failure like RETRY_HANDOFF and the gateway re-resolves owner and retries. avoids blocking latency yet fixes correctness.
maria: prefer a typed error so gateway can route without treating as internal failure. like ReplyCode::RETRY_HANDOFF. gateway will attempt single re-route to new owner.
kevin: need to be strict about only doing this for idempotent/read-only RPCs. non-idempotent ops must continue to be serialized.
sara: agreed. let's gate the surface: read/get, scan, embed-fetch can return retry; mutate ops get FULL_EVICT or a harder stall.
aj: implementation sketch:
```
enum ReplyCode { OK, RETRY_HANDOFF, NOT_SAFE }
// fastpath
if (pin_epoch != current_epoch && handoff_active) return RETRY_HANDOFF
```
kevin: also include an optional header `x-pref-epoch` in responses so gateway can decide if it needs to re-resolve without extra lookup.
evans: testing: unit to simulate epoch flip at response time, integration canary that injects artificial revoke during reads. I'll make a harness.
maria: metrics: add `prefix.handoff_retries` and `prefix.handoff_conflicts_rate`. ops-bot, can you add dashboards and an alert for sustained >10/min?
ops-bot: added metric placeholders + grafana panel. alert rule created: prefix.handoff_retries > 10/min over 5m.
sara: rollout plan: behind a feature flag `evict_handoff_retry` default false. enable on small canary pool, monitor metrics and error budget.
aj: gateway change required: on RETRY_HANDOFF, call owner-discovery and forward once. add safety: only retry once, then surface error to client.
kevin: doc note: clarify that clients may see a routed retry for read paths during handoff; update API docs to say reads are retried once transparently.
evans: concern: some read workflows expect strict linearizability. this retry preserves safety because new owner will have latest state; but add a note in README about edge-case invariants.
maria: long-term idea: make handoff atomic by briefly quiescing new pins for a short window (20-200ms) at swap point. that would remove retries but increases p99. we'll table for now.
sara: decision: implement cheap epoch recheck + RETRY_HANDOFF for read-only RPCs, feature-flagged. gateway single re-route. metrics and canary plan in place.
aj: I'll draft runtime/GW patches. evans will write tests. maria will own canary.
maria: opening PRs today. thanks all :thumbsup:
